text:
It is only with the heart that one can see rightly; 
what is essential is invisible to the eye.
source: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry, The Little Prince

text:
All grown-ups were once children...
but only few of them remember it.
source: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry, The Little Prince

text: We see the world not as it is, but as we are.
insights:
Every observation passes through memory, expectation, and mood. Recognizing that filter does not make perception useless; it makes us more humble about what we think we know.

A useful practice is to ask what another person might be seeing from where they stand.

text: A little progress each day adds up to something remarkable.
insights:
Consistency rarely feels dramatic while it is happening. Its power becomes visible only after many ordinary efforts have accumulated.

Make the next step small enough to repeat, not impressive enough to exhaust you.

text: Let curiosity lead where certainty cannot.
insights:
Certainty closes a question; curiosity keeps it alive. When the path is unclear, a sincere question often moves us farther than a confident assumption.

Follow what makes you want to look twice.

text: Begin before you feel completely ready.
insights:
Readiness is often produced by beginning, not achieved before it. The first attempt exposes the real questions and replaces imagined difficulty with useful evidence.

Start gently, then let experience teach you what preparation could not.

text: Make room for the life that is trying to find you.
insights:
Growth sometimes asks for space before it offers a clear destination. Releasing an old habit, obligation, or expectation can be an active form of preparation.

Not every empty space needs to be filled immediately.

text: Do the next small thing, then the next.
insights:
Large goals become workable when attention returns to the action directly in front of us. You do not need to carry the whole journey at once.

Choose a concrete step, finish it, and allow completion to reveal the next one.

text: Your future is shaped by what you practice today.
insights:
Practice is a quiet vote for the person you are becoming. Repeated actions build ability, but they also build identity.

Spend time on what you hope will feel natural tomorrow.

text: Momentum begins with one honest attempt.
insights:
An honest attempt does not guarantee success; it creates contact with reality. That contact provides feedback, and feedback gives the next attempt a direction.

Motion needs less certainty than hesitation demands.

text: A meaningful life is built in ordinary moments.
insights:
Meaning does not live only in milestones. It gathers through attention, care, and participation in days that may appear unremarkable from the outside.

How we inhabit common moments eventually becomes the shape of a life.

text: What we give our attention to becomes our world.
insights:
Attention is limited, and its repeated direction determines what feels prominent and real. This makes attention both a resource and a responsibility.

Notice what your habits keep placing at the center of your experience.

text: Enough is not a quantity; it is a way of seeing.
insights:
More cannot settle a question that has no finish line. Enough begins when we can recognize value without immediately measuring what is missing.

Contentment and ambition can coexist when ambition is not asked to prove our worth.
